#### 1. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4E  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.777)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9619665, Reactome:R-HSA-381340, Reactome:R-HSA-5617472, Reactome:R-HSA-9031628)

Mutations in EGR2 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting the normal transcription of myelin-related genes and impairing Schwann cell differentiation. This disruption in myelin gene expression ultimately results in the peripheral neuropathy characteristic of Charcot-Marie-Tooth diseases, and in some cases, cerebellar hypoplasia.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in EGR2 were found to cause a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or if the causal genes for the two diseases were completely distinct and non-overlapping in their downstream pathways, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD revealing common variants (AF > 0.1%) in the coding sequence of EGR2 would challenge its role as a causal gene for rare Mendelian diseases, though this is unlikely for known CMT genes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism mediated by EGR2 haploinsufficiency could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring EGR2 function or compensating for its loss, potentially benefiting patients with both CMT1D and CMT4E.
